jobs.description:
Company Description
Giving Tree Surrogacy is a world-class surrogacy agency dedicated to helping intended parents, surrogates, and egg donors achieve their family-building goals through compassionate, comprehensive support. The organization is built on the belief that providing care and guidance brings purpose and lasting fulfillment to everyone involved in the surrogacy journey. A dedicated and experienced team offers personalized resources, education, and advocacy to help minimize stress and address concerns at every step. Giving Tree Surrogacy focuses on delivering professional expertise and high-level, individualized support to create a positive and rewarding experience for all parties. The agency is committed to guiding each person through a safe, informed, and successful journey toward fulfilling their dreams.

Role Description
This is a full-time REMOTE role for a BILINGUAL Surrogacy Case Manager (English + Mandarin). The Surrogacy Case Manager will serve as the primary point of contact for intended parents, surrogates, and other stakeholders, providing guidance, updates, and support throughout the surrogacy process. Daily responsibilities include managing case timelines and milestones, scheduling appointments and meetings, and facilitating communication among medical professionals, legal partners, and clients. The role involves tracking documentation, ensuring compliance with internal procedures and external guidelines, and promptly addressing questions or concerns with empathy and professionalism. The Surrogacy Case Manager will also support educational efforts, maintain accurate records in case management systems, and collaborate with the broader team to continuously enhance the client experience.

Native speaker level in English and Mandarin
Strong case management and organizational skills, including the ability to prioritize tasks, manage multiple cases simultaneously, and meet deadlines in a dynamic environment.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex processes clearly and build trust with individuals from diverse backgrounds.
Demonstrated empathy, emotional intelligence, and conflict-resolution skills to support clients through sensitive and emotionally charged situations.
Experience working in surrogacy, fertility, healthcare, social work, counseling, or a related field is highly beneficial.
Comfort with remote work tools and technology, including case management software, video conferencing platforms, and standard office applications.
Attention to detail and strong documentation skills to maintain accurate records, track progress, and support compliance with procedures and applicable regulations.

jobs.title: Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Organization Description: 

Colorado Food Cluster (CFC) Inc. partners with community organizations throughout Colorado to provide critical support, resources and services to students and their families. Through culturally responsive approaches, CFC provides nutritious meals to children and families throughout Colorado leveraging federally funded programs. CFC continuously seeks opportunities and programs that remove barriers to access food, for all people in our communities using innovative solutions to improve access to nutritious food.

Job Overview:

The Program Coordinator will support the successful implementation of the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) and Summer Food Service Program (SFSP), ensuring CFC meets applicable federal and state requirements as a Sponsor organization. The Coordinator will  support program implementation, day-to-day operations, and continued development of CFC’s newest Medicaid meal delivery program.

The Program Coordinator will manage a variety of daily administrative and program responsibilities, including recordkeeping, partner onboarding and support, site visits, program audits, service expansion, and communications. The Program Coordinator will work closely with partners to ensure they have the information and resources needed to successfully provide services while meeting required program timelines and deadlines.

The Program Coordinator must be able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment and support CFC programs as needs evolve throughout the year. Travel to different regions of Colorado will be required.

This position includes a 30-day introductory period, after which the employee becomes eligible for health insurance benefits.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Support planning and coordination of ongoing programs and activities for CACFP, Home Delivered Meals through Medicaid, and SFSP.
Proactively and independently manage assigned daily tasks, projects, and program deadlines.
Maintain an understanding of rules, regulations, and policies applicable to Federal Nutrition Programs, stay current on updated requirements, and interpret operational impacts.
Design systems and structures for effective program implementation and expansion efforts for CACFP, Medicaid, and SFSP.
Support monthly CACFP and SFSP claim preparation, including review and reconciliation of attendance, meal counts, enrollment records, Income Eligibility Forms, menus, production records, and other required documentation.
Identify missing, incomplete, expired, or noncompliant documentation and communicate necessary corrections to participating sites prior to claim submission.
Track claim deadlines and required program submissions to ensure timely and accurate reporting.
Support preparation and organization of program records for state reviews, audits, and other oversight activities.
Conduct required federal onsite monitoring visits to providers and caretakers across Colorado, including but not limited to home care providers, afterschool programs, and childcare centers.
Document monitoring findings and communicate required follow-up or corrective actions to participating sites when applicable.
Coordinate with food vendors regarding menus, meal orders, delivery schedules, substitutions, documentation, service issues, and program compliance.
Train and onboard new centers, home providers, vendors, and other partners on CFC processes, documentation requirements, program systems, meal service procedures, and applicable program requirements.
Maintain consistent follow-up with partners regarding outstanding documentation, deadlines, compliance issues, and operational changes.
Engage partners to inform them of program offerings and enroll students, centers, and home providers in meal delivery programs.
Work with community organizations to inform them about programming and support enrollment efforts.
Identify and manage partners with aligned missions and priorities.
Manage daily email and phone communications in the CRM system from families accessing programming.
Support families with program registration platforms and troubleshoot issues.
Develop and disseminate high-quality communications to support program implementation and expansion.
Facilitate external presentations about CFC programs for multiple audiences.
Support development and distribution of external communications, including but not limited to newsletters, social media, and customer service communications.
Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications and Experiences: 

Bachelor's degree or relevant years of experience. 
Registered Dietitian or Certified Nutritionist credential required to support Medicaid program requirements.
2+ of experience working with communities. 
Excellent organizational and time management skills.
Detail-oriented and efficient.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong attention to detail and demonstrated ability to review documentation for accuracy and completeness.
Ability to communicate expectations, deadlines, and compliance concerns professionally with external partners.
Ability to execute projects from development phase to operation.
Experience implementing public programming preferably programs funded through federal funds.
Ability to work independently in a remote work environment while maintaining consistent communication, documentation, and accountability.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines while maintaining accurate and organized records.
Have access to reliable transportation.
Have a valid drivers license.
Ability to travel to all areas of Colorado as needed.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience:

Candidates who are bilingual are strongly encouraged to apply.
Focus and special interest in food insecurity, childcare and policy.
Experience with CACFP, SFSP, Medicaid, or other federal/state nutrition or human services programs. 
Proficiency working in Google Suite.
Problem Solver.
Strong understanding of community engagement strategies.

The Harris Center for Mental Health and IDD
(“The HARRIS CENTER”) is looking for a Peer Support Specialist

Overview

Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center is an independent, nonprofit organization providing adult cancer treatment and groundbreaking research focused on cancer and infectious diseases. Based in Seattle, Fred Hutch is the only National Cancer Institute-designated cancer center in Washington.

With a track record of global leadership in bone marrow transplantation, HIV/AIDS prevention, immunotherapy and COVID-19 vaccines, Fred Hutch has earned a reputation as one of the world’s leading cancer, infectious disease and biomedical research centers. Fred Hutch operates eight clinical care sites that provide medical oncology, infusion, radiation, proton therapy and related services, and network affiliations with hospitals in five states. Together, our fully integrated research and clinical care teams seek to discover new cures to the world’s deadliest diseases and make life beyond cancer a reality.

At Fred Hutch we value collaboration, compassion, determination, excellence, innovation, integrity and respect. Our mission is directly tied to the humanity, dignity and inherent value of each employee, patient, community member and supporter. Our commitment to learning across our differences and similarities make us stronger. We seek employees who bring different and innovative ways of seeing the world and solving problems.

The Acute Care Social Worker provides direct social work services to patients and their families. This position is responsible for the assessment of the patient/family's psychosocial needs. About The Role

Adults Social Worker - South Essex (Expression of Interest)

Permanent, Full Time

Register your interest here to be notified of upcoming Social Worker opportunities within Essex County Council's Adult Social Care services in South Essex. The starting salary for a NQSW is £36,124 per annum, rising to £38,487 per annum upon successful completion of the ASYE programme.

About Our Social Worker Roles

We’re an adult social care service that wants to see citizens of Essex have as much choice and control over the way they live their lives as possible. We think everyone should have the chance to live a full and fulfilling life with people they love and care about, doing things that matter to them and living in a place they can call home. We’re determined that with the right support, everyone can maintain or achieve some independence and we’re proud to be working to make these ambitions a reality.

Our Social Workers work alongside people and their families and carers to help them think through what might help them get on with their lives in the way that works best for them. We do this within the framework of our statutory Care Act requirements. This means many of our conversations are framed as ‘assessments’, ‘reviews’, ‘support planning’ and ‘safeguarding’. But our aim is always to listen and understand what matters to the person and then to work with them to think through how this might be achieved.

The teams in South Essex are primarily based out of our offices in Basildon. South Essex borders the unitary authority of Southend and Thurrock and offers the opportunity to work with health partners within the area. In addition, the area also has good links to London. With a mix of Urban and some rural/ semi-rural locations, the variety and scope of the work you will be able to get involved in is huge.

Take a look at our short video here to get a glimpse into the role and what it’s like to be a Social Worker at Essex County Council.

About You

If you share our vision, enjoy meeting people and hearing their stories you might be interested to find out more about what we do.

If you’re also a Social Worker registered with Social Work England with that winning combination of creative thought, reliability and practical ability to get things done, we’d really love to hear from you!

You’ll have a broad understanding of our statutory responsibilities and a commitment to meeting these in a person-centred way.

“The local authority had a good structure and processes in place to enable people to be supported successfully, and support people to remain independent and live healthy lives. The workforce was passionate about supporting people to achieve these outcomes and the local authority had good knowledge of their area, the people living there and the demographics.”

You can read the full report on the CQC website here.

Our teams are busy but warm, friendly and supportive. Our fabulous team managers will help you manage your workload and develop your practice.

We take your career just as seriously as you do, and we have a continuing professional development offer that’s second to none.

We welcome diversity because it makes us grow and we’re determined to become a fully inclusive and an anti-racist organisation.

We’ll support you to be your best and will offer:

Ongoing opportunities for continuing professional development
Flexible working options
Employee wellbeing and counselling
Lease Car scheme
Life assurance of three times annual salary
Local Government Pension Scheme. View Key Facts and FAQ’s about the LGPS.
Volunteering leave
27 days annual leave (plus bank holidays), rising with service
Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) - access to free and confidential information, support, and guidance from a team of highly qualified professionals.
Employee Networks – communities to support you, connect you and help influence change at ECC
Payment of your Social Work England registration fees!

Whatever you want to achieve in your social work career, you can do it here.

T&Cs Apply.

Apply now.

For more information contact Abbie.Mollison@essex.gov.uk

You can read more about devolution and local government reorganisation (LGR)) on our careers site

Once you’ve secured your role within Essex County Council you will receive many great employee benefits, including support for unpaid carers and flexible working arrangements to accommodate their needs.

At Essex County Council, we value integrity and ethical behaviour. We kindly ask that you embrace our code of conduct and the Nolan principles, including throughout the recruitment process. Your commitment to these standards helps us maintain a positive and respectful workplace for everyone.
